title: Kitchen Renovation Cost Estimator | UK Guide
description: Use our kitchen renovation cost estimator to plan cabinets, worktops, appliances, fitting and structural work, then prepare for an accurate local quote.

blocks.text: A kitchen renovation cost estimator is useful for setting a realistic budget before you choose units, appliances or finishes. In the UK, the total can vary considerably: replacing doors and worktops is a very different project from moving walls, renewing electrics and plumbing, and fitting a completely new kitchen. This guide breaks the cost into the main parts so homeowners in Hertfordshire, North London and Bedfordshire can compare options and ask for a more accurate local quote.
How to use a kitchen renovation cost estimator

Start with the size and layout of the room, then list each cost category separately. As a rough UK planning guide, a straightforward small or medium kitchen renovation might typically cost around £8,000 to £20,000, while a larger or more customised project may exceed £25,000. Every project differs, so these are broad planning figures rather than quotations; get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. The final price depends on the number of units, chosen materials, appliance specification, access to the property, preparation work and whether VAT is included in the figures you receive.

items: Cabinetry: the number of cupboards, drawers, tall units, corner solutions and any bespoke storage.
Worktops and splashbacks: material, thickness, cut-outs, joints and upstands.
Appliances: integrated or freestanding models, extraction, installation and disposal of old appliances.
Fitting: removal, preparation, cabinet installation, worktops, plumbing, electrics, tiling and decorating.
Structural work: walls, windows, doors, flooring, ceilings, gas or plumbing alterations and electrical upgrades.
Additional costs: delivery, waste removal, building control where applicable, and VAT if it is not already included.

Cabinets are often a significant product cost. Flat-pack and entry-level ranges may suit a tight budget, while rigid, made-to-measure or bespoke units generally cost more. As a rough UK guide, units for a simple run of cabinets might typically cost around £2,000 to £6,000, while a larger kitchen with tall housings, an island, internal storage and premium finishes may cost £10,000 or more. Every project differs, so obtain a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. Check whether doors, handles, plinths, end panels, fillers and internal drawers are included, as these items can be left out of an initial headline price.
Worktop costs can change the estimate quickly

Laminate is often a lower-cost worktop option. As a rough UK allowance, it may typically cost around £500 to £1,500 for many standard kitchens. Timber, solid-surface, quartz and natural stone may typically range from around £1,500 to £5,000 or more, depending on the area, edge detail and number of cut-outs. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. Sink and hob openings, joints, drainer grooves and templating may be charged separately. If you are comparing estimates, make sure every quote describes the same worktop material and includes fitting.

As a rough UK guide, appliances may typically add around £1,500 to £6,000 to a kitchen budget, although premium or specialist choices can cost more. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. A typical list may include an oven, hob, extractor, fridge-freezer, dishwasher and washing machine. Integrated appliances can require additional housing panels and careful coordination with the cabinet layout. Ask whether delivery, connection, testing and removal of existing appliances are included. Electrical or gas connections should be carried out by suitably qualified professionals, with the necessary documentation provided where relevant.

As a rough UK guide, fitting for a standard kitchen might typically cost around £3,000 to £7,000, but the range is wide because the scope can include more than placing cabinets in position. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing. A detailed quote should identify removal of the old kitchen, protection of floors and surfaces, assembly, levelling, scribing, worktop fitting, appliance installation, plumbing, electrical work, tiling, flooring and decorating. A kitchen with a simple replacement layout is usually less labour-intensive than one where services must be moved or several trades need to work in sequence.

Structural changes can make an estimator less reliable until the property has been assessed. Removing a partition, creating an opening, moving a doorway or altering a window can add substantially to the budget, particularly where structural design, approvals or specialist work are needed. You may also need to allow for floor repairs, damp or uneven walls, new plasterboard, upgraded circuits, additional sockets, ventilation, plumbing runs, heating changes or ceiling repairs. Before accepting a fixed price, ask who is responsible for investigating hidden defects and how unexpected work will be priced.
How to obtain an accurate local kitchen quote

items: Provide measurements, photographs and a simple plan showing doors, windows, radiators, boiler locations, water points and existing sockets.
Explain whether the layout is staying the same or whether you want an island, changed appliances, moved plumbing or removed walls.
Choose a specification before comparing prices: cabinet range, worktop, handles, sink, tap, appliances, flooring, splashback and lighting.
Ask for labour, materials, delivery, waste disposal, preparation and VAT to be shown clearly rather than relying on one total.

faq.q: How much does a kitchen renovation cost in the UK?
faq.a: As a rough UK guide, a straightforward renovation might typically cost around £8,000 to £20,000, while larger, premium or structurally altered kitchens may exceed £25,000. Every project differs, so get a free, no-obligation quote for accurate pricing.

faq.q: What is the biggest cost in a kitchen renovation?
faq.a: Cabinetry and fitting can be significant costs, followed by worktops and appliances. Structural changes, service relocation and hidden repairs can have a major effect on the final total.

faq.q: How can I reduce my kitchen renovation cost?
faq.a: Keeping the existing layout, choosing standard-size cabinets, comparing worktop materials and reusing suitable appliances can reduce costs. Avoid cutting corners on electrical, plumbing or structural work.

faq.q: What should a kitchen fitting quote include?
faq.a: It should set out removal, preparation, cabinet and worktop fitting, appliance connections, plumbing, electrics, tiling, flooring, waste disposal, delivery, VAT and any exclusions or allowances.

faq.q: How do I get an accurate kitchen renovation estimate?
faq.a: Arrange a site visit and provide measurements, photographs, your preferred layout and a specification of finishes and appliances. A written quote should then separate products, labour and potential additional work.
